result.result:
The app is built and working in `app/`. Start it with `npx @angular/cli@19 serve` from `app/` and log in with `admin` / `admin`. The production build has no errors or warnings. I wrote a Playwright script that drives the whole flow in a real browser (`qa/e2e.mjs`), and it passed on three runs in a row with no console errors.

**What the script covers:**
- **Login:** empty and wrong-password submits show field errors; a correct login writes `isLoggedIn` to `localStorage` and lands on the dashboard.
- **Guards:** a logged-in user sent to `/login` goes to the dashboard; after sign-out, `/users` goes back to login.
- **Dashboard:** all 8 tiles and 7 bars render, and the log viewer adds a new line every 3 seconds.
- **Profile menu:** opens leftward and stays fully on screen at both 1280px and 375px wide; closes on an outside click.
- **Users:** the 5 seed records load. Details closes on a backdrop click. Edit splits the name, saves and the table updates. "Delete user" in the edit dialog opens the delete confirmation with the same member, and deleting removes the row. Invite validates all four fields, then adds the new member.

**How it's put together:** all colours, spacing, font sizes, radii and shadows come from the Figma file and live as variables in `src/styles.css`. Components only use those variables; the few remaining raw numbers are screen-width breakpoints. Badges, avatars and the dialog frame are shared components.

**Where Figma and the spec disagreed, I followed the spec's content and Figma's styling:**
- **Login card:** Figma also shows a "Blueprint" heading, different wording and a divider. I used exactly the 7 elements the spec lists.
- **Dashboard layout:**
  - Figma has 4 metric tiles, a 538/658px split row, then a full-width logs card. In the split row, Service Health is on the left and Request Throughput on the right, as in Figma, even though the spec lists Throughput first.
  - Figma has no separate Data Summary tile, so I added one as a full-width row of stats.
  - I kept Figma's "System Overview" heading above the tiles.
  - Tile titles are uppercase because the spec says so; Figma's are not.
- **Text:** tile values, service names and day labels follow the spec rather than Figma's sample text.
- **Error Rate trend badge:** red, not Figma's amber, because the spec says it should read as negative.
- **Logs:** a dark, monospace terminal panel as the spec asks. Figma shows a light list with coloured dots.
- **Users table:** separate Avatar and Name columns as the spec asks. Figma combines them into one "User" column. Action order and emphasis follow the spec: Details is plain, Edit is outlined, Delete is red-outlined.
- **Header:** the nav links are "Dashboard" and "Team Members" so they point at real routes; Figma shows Overview / Metrics / Logs / Settings. I left out the "Online" badge Figma shows in the header, because the spec doesn't list it.
- **Footer:** Figma has only a copyright line and two legal links. I added the brand and link columns the spec requires, styled to match.

**Visual choices I couldn't confirm from the design data:**
- The design data lists dividers and card borders as pure black, which looks like a lost transparency setting, so I used the light grey border colour the header and table use.
- The logo, the profile menu, the size of the delete dialog, the layout at narrow widths, the throughput numbers and the colours inside the log panel are all my own choices.
- The Inter and JetBrains Mono fonts load from Google Fonts.

During testing I fixed one real bug: Save changes and Send Invite didn't submit, because those forms weren't wired to their form controls. I also stopped the header from overflowing at 375px wide. The `qa/` folder holds the test script, its screenshots and its own Playwright install; it isn't part of the app and you can delete it.
